description.value: Red Cedar Café is a registered non-profit community meal program founded in April 2020 in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, operating out of a commercial kitchen at 1900 Douglas Street in Victoria. It prepares around 1,000 free or pay-what-you-can frozen meals weekly — vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options included — and runs a Free Store distributing produce, bread, and groceries from the same location. A touring cyclist in need of accessible food support will find a welcoming, volunteer-run operation rooted in mutual aid principles.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms Red Cedar Café is a real, operating non-profit community meal program at 1900 Douglas Street, Victoria, BC V8T 4K8, phone (778) 817-0395 — neither address nor phone appear in the OSM record. Vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options are explicitly stated on the /our-programs and /donate pages. No mention of bike parking, washrooms, Wi-Fi, or water refill is made anywhere on the site.
concerns: OSM tags this as amenity=restaurant, but it is a registered non-profit community meal program with limited public-facing hours (Free Store one morning per week); the restaurant tag is misleading.
OSM name is 'Red Cedar Cafe' (no accent); website consistently uses 'Red Cedar Café' (with accent on é).
OSM record contains no address or phone number; both were sourced from the website.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, operating, publicly accessible community food program at a confirmed physical address in Victoria; a touring cyclist in need of accessible food support can benefit from it.
enrichment_extras.notes: All meals are free or pay-what-you-can. The frozen meal program is primarily delivery-based; the Free Store is the walk-in access point. This organization may be more relevant to cyclists in food-insecure situations than to general touring cyclists.

Vegetarian / vegan / GF.detail: Website states: 'We provide vegetarian, vegan, and gluten free options where possible' and 'Our weekly menus offer meat-based, vegetarian, gluten-free and vegan options.'
